articles.title: Golden State Valkyries v Atlanta Dream: WNBA finals 2026 Game 6 – live
articles.summary: Dream host Valkyries in opener of best-of-seven series. Dream say concerns went unheeded for 12.30pm start. Reach out to Ella on Bluesky or by email. Valkyries 5-8 Dream, 6.41, first quarter.
body: “We know if we don’t keep it up, we go home,” Dream guard Allisha Gray says in the half-time interview. “I’m not ready for my season to be over yet.”

Golden State found some momentum at the end of the second quarter, getting a three-pointer from Tiffany Hayes and then a layup from Laeticia Amihere off an Atlanta turnover. Those were the Valkyries’ first points off a turnover of the game. The Dream went the final three minutes of the quarter without scoring, but their 20-point lead is comfortable heading into the second half.

It’s too soon to say we’re certainly headed to a Game 7, but it feels like the Dream are one big run from putting this one away. They have more made three-pointers (eight) than Golden State have made field goals (seven). Rhyne Howard has 11 points and went 3-for-5 from deep. Hayes leads the Valkyries with 11, but as a team they are just 26% from the field.

The Valkyries missed three layups in a span of two minutes, which just about sums up their first half. Meanwhile, this sums up Atlanta’s first half: the Dream are 15-0 (!) this season when Angel Reese hits at least one three-pointer. The record for a half-time lead in the WNBA finals is 22 points.

articles.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
articles.summary: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma. By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been.
body: And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings.
Yet, apparently, a crisis of a sort has been churning just below the surface of what is, by broad consensus, Europe’s best home support.

On Friday, Dortmund had announced a kind of bribery scheme. A rewards program is probably a kinder way of putting it. Fans who stayed off their phones during the bout with Eintracht had the chance to win signed jerseys and earn gift cards to the club’s merchandise store. If they activated a so-called “fan mode” on the club’s app – a name so phenomenally passive-aggressive you can only applaud whoever came up with it – the club could count who unlocked their phones the fewest times during the game. For every minute the fans left their phones alone, they got points.
Dortmund are not the only German team to pick a fight with phones.

The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma.

articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli is to miss Thursday's Mexico City Grand Prix media day with an illness as he stands on the brink of clinching his first world title.
body: The Italian's Mercedes team said that Antonelli had a "viral illness" and had been excused his duties on Thursday by governing body the FIA "as a precaution to give him the chance to rest ahead of the weekend".

Antonelli will seal the championship, and become the youngest winner in Formula 1 history, as long as he does not lose more than two points to team-mate George Russell and one point to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in the grand prix on Sunday.
The only way he could be stopped from tying up the title is if one of Russell and Hamilton wins. Ninth would be enough for Antonelli to become champion if it is Russell, and 10th if it is Hamilton.
Antonelli is one of two drivers to miss media day with an illness.

articles.title: DC United are worse than awful; they’re hopeless
articles.summary: The team have gone from MLS’s flagship franchise to their most depressing – even among 2026’s other stragglers. Sign up for our free newsletter here. For years, the crisp air and changing colors of October brought forth a host of wonderful memories for DC United fans – visions of Eddie Pope heading…
body: Nowadays, United fans have a different tradition: hearing the team’s ownership apologize for yet another depressing season and offer promises of a brighter future. With Wednesday night’s 2-1 loss to Toronto, United will now miss out on the playoffs for the seventh consecutive season – in a league that lets at least 50% of teams into the playoffs each year, with 60% of teams or more making it in five of those seven years. If United fail to make it again next year, they’ll tie an all-time MLS record.

United have cycled through coaches, players and staff at a dizzying rate in recent years; their most recent attempt to right the ship involved hiring René Weiler, a Swiss journeyman who has guided 10 clubs in a 20-year coaching career. United’s choice to lead its sporting department felt even more bizarre: they hired Dr Erkut Sogut, a German-born lawyer and sports agent who had never worked in a front office before, with Wikipedia saying he is “most notable for being the agent of football star Mesut Özil”. Sogut – who has also penned a number of books about the “high-octane” world of “football and the powerful agents who control it” – has yet to turn things around, even a little bit.

articles.title: Bears swing big and trade two first-round picks for star Titans DT Jeffery Simmons
articles.summary: Struggling Tennessee get haul of picks for tackle. Chicago are chasing first Super Bowl title since 1985. The Chicago Bears have acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans, a person familiar with the deal told the Associated Press on Thursday.
body: The Bears sent their first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, along with a fourth-rounder in next year’s draft, to the Titans for Simmons and a fifth-round selection in 2028.
The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal had not been announced.

Led by Caleb Williams, Chicago have won two in a row to improve to 5-2 going into Monday night’s game at Seattle. They are chasing the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North, and the addition of Simmons bolsters what had a been a questionable defensive line.

The Bears won the division last year for the first time since 2018, finishing with an 11-6 record in coach Ben Johnson’s first season in charge. They advanced in the playoffs by edging the Green Bay Packers in a wild-card game before losing to the Los Angeles Rams in overtime in the divisional round.

articles.title: Celtic & Rangers Scottish Cup stadium closure upheld
articles.summary: Rangers and Celtic will both play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors after the clubs respective appeals against the sanction was dismissed.
body: The Glasgow clubs presented their cases to a Scottish FA appellate tribunal on Monday, but have failed to overturn a ban on supporters.
They will also be required to pay £100,000 to the visiting club in their respective home ties in the national cup competition.
However, a suspended ban on fans in the case of further infractions was set aside by the tribunal.
The stadium closure penalty was announced in late August following the disorder at the end of last season's quarter-final tie at Ibrox, which Celtic won after a penalty shoot-out.

articles.title: Duckett, Dawson star as England hold off Sri Lanka for consolation win
articles.summary: Ben Duckett fired the highest score of his ODI career to help England end a disappointing tri-series campaign with a 55-run victory over Sri Lanka in Lahore.
body: England's hopes of reaching Saturday's final in Pakistan were already over after three consecutive group stage defeats, but Harry Brook's side successfully defended a commanding target of 387 and claimed a consolation win.
Duckett fired 167 from just 132 deliveries and put on big partnerships with Tom Banton (74) and Brook (44), as England scored 386-5 after losing the toss and batting first.

Pavan Rathnayake led the reply with 118 from 77 deliveries and Kusal Mendis (89) also impressed, with Sri Lanka threatening to pull off another famous chase - like they managed against England last week - when they passed 300 with five wickets still in hand.

Liam Dawson (4-49) made the Rathnayake breakthrough and Sonny Baker (2-75) also took key wickets, while Henry Crocombe, Joe Root and Sam Curran claimed one each, as Sri Lanka were dismissed for 331 after 45.1 overs.

articles.title: Westlake football vs Cedar Ridge: 3 things to watch in Austin-area clash Friday
articles.summary: There are no official district championship games in Texas high school football, but when Westlake hosts Cedar Ridge Friday, it's about as close as it can get. At least a share of the District 25-6A title will be on the line as the top two teams in the American-Statesman's 6A power rankings clash.
body: Cedar Ridge (8-0, 4-0), which is arguably one of the most surprising teams in the state, puts its undefeated record on the line against a Chaps team that may have been underrated - by Westlake standards - in the preseason.
Here are three things to watch and a prediction for the biggest regular-season matchup in Central Texas this season.

Westlake (7-1, 4-0) doesn't need to be flashy on offense because it can simply line up and run the ball straight at opponents, as evidenced by its win over Lake Travis. That's due to a combination of things, but mainly an offensive line that might have five starters who could play at some level in college. Running back CJ Jones is a budding star with already more than 30 Power 4 offers, and quarterback Patton Jones is a true dual threat who would thrive running the option if needed.

Cedar Ridge has two of the area's best defensive players in the front seven in defensive tackle Jeremiah Passmore and linebacker Ayden O'Brien Brown. They'll be key in trying to force Westlake into third-and-long situations, giving talented defensive backs Trent Bell and Bekett Lohman opportunities to make plays against the pass.

articles.summary: Darnell Ridgeway is looking to bring another professional athlete to the Maple City to coach up Hornell area youth. Ridgeway, founder of Coach Ridge Events LLC in Hornell, is planning a youth wrestling camp featuring Olympic gold medalist and WWE legend Kurt Angle on Feb.
body: During the camp, kids will rotate through wrestling stations led by local coaches and high school wrestlers, working on fundamentals, building confidence, and connecting with other young athletes. Each registered participant also gets a photo and autograph with Kurt Angle, Ridgeway said.

"Through Coach Ridge’s Elite Combine, my goal is to bring big-time opportunities to small-town kids — giving families in Hornell and surrounding communities access to memorable experiences with professional athletes close to home," said Ridgeway.
The event welcomes boys and girls ages 6-16, from Hornell and all surrounding communities, regardless of experience level. The cost is $160 per athlete, with capacity limited to the first 80.
Ridgeway currently has 25 kids registered for the camp, and needs at least 60 by Dec. 1 for the event to move forward.

articles.title: Is Kalshi Legal in California? October 2026 Legal Status and How to Trade
articles.summary: Is Kalshi legal in California? Yes. Kalshi is a CFTC regulated exchange open to Californians 18+. Get the legal status, tribal lands ruling and FOXSPORTS55 offer.
body: Is Kalshi legal in California? Yes, Kalshi is legal and available in California because it operates as a Designated Contract Market regulated by the federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), not as a California licensed sportsbook. That distinction matters in a state where online sports betting is still not legal, and it is also why Kalshi's sports contracts are the subject of an active court fight involving three California tribes.

Kalshi is legal in California. The platform accepts sign-ups from California residents, the state has taken no enforcement action against it, and Californians aged 18 and older can create an account, deposit, and trade event contracts on sports, politics, economics, weather, and culture.

The honest caveat is that the sports side of the platform is under active litigation. Kalshi has voluntarily disabled its markets on the lands of three California tribes following a September 2026 Ninth Circuit ruling, and the broader question of whether states can regulate sports event contracts is heading toward the U.S. Supreme Court. None of that blocks Californians statewide today.
